proposal.falsifier: Falsified by any of the following, observed in a fresh episode executed from task entry on a frozen source set: (a) the fingerprint step shows that latch kind, source-segment structure, dt, shunt list and capacitance default are numerically identical to a prior episode AND a band freshly derived here contradicts a band carried from that episode, yet the carried band would have selected the delivering design (the precaution would then be provably unnecessary and its cost unjustified); (b) a design chosen by the discrete-grid predictor with all three logged margins positive and validated to within two dt ticks fails to deliver exactly one 8-byte frame by receive_deadline_s, while some legal design satisfying the same logged inequalities is observed to deliver (the selection rule is wrong); (c) after validation within two dt ticks, the predictor still misses the observed t_boot or t_done of the executed design by more than two dt ticks (the discrete formulation is still wrong, so revert to the base method and log the residuals); (d) a post-terminal event triggers a knob change, a new execution, or a changed diagnosis (the terminality rule is violated); (e) an achieved packet with the required bytes, a unique event id and time <= deadline is re-labelled a failure, or a budget/tool error is answered by re-sending an identical payload (discipline violated and cost paid twice); (f) the procedure changes two knobs in one execution, edits the task, physics, initial state, evaluator or budget, or reports the outcome as hardware validity, statistical advantage, migration, recursive self-improvement or external acceptance. Any (a)-(f) means the update is rejected in favour of base H, with the mismatch, the residuals and the executions actually spent recorded.
proposal.hypothesis: If H is consumed from task entry, then four changes each prevent a failure mode that is visible in the retained record rather than hypothetical. (1) Fingerprinting the acquired fields before any diagnosis prevents importing a design band from a sibling episode: the retained episodes share world id b-transient-behavior-v1 but differ in event_latch ('volatile' vs 'passive-mechanical'), in source structure (two segments 0-0.006 s at 16.667 mW plus 0.03-0.06 s at 3.667 mW with a shunt, vs a single segment 0-0.02 s at 7.5 mW) and in the capacitance default (1e-5 F vs 2.2e-5 F), so a band or floor remembered from one scenario is mis-specified in the other. (2) Terminality-first reading prevents diagnosing expected decay as failure: one retained trace already contains an 8-byte delivery at 0.0158 s followed by a brownout at 0.3395 s after the source segment ended, and reacting to it by lowering capacitance or raising the transmit floor moves in exactly the direction that produced zero frames in the other retained trace (capture at 0.0037-0.0079 s destroyed by an energy-threshold brownout at 0.0121 s). (3) Stating the predictor as discrete per-tick operations and matching it against a fingerprint-matched recorded trace before spending a candidate keeps forecast error inside two dt ticks; the retained closed form ceil((E_ready+boot_j)/charge_step) predicted 0.0166 s against an observed 0.0158 s, an eight-tick miss that was a formula defect, not a design defect. (4) One knob per execution, in the sign direction of the violated inequality, plus at most one send attempt per distinct payload, avoids both an uninformative two-knob trial and the duplicate re-send that consumed a retained episode's residual budget (identical payload rejected twice as EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT). Net effect: an execution is spent only when a logged inequality is violated, an achieved design is retained unchanged, and UNKNOWNs and costs stay recorded. This is a procedural claim about method consumption under the frozen public model and public sources only; physical calibration is UNKNOWN and acceptance is external.
proposal.method_text:
H update v3: fingerprint -> terminality -> discrete predictor -> validated selection. Every statement is a prediction about consumption of the frozen public model and the acquired public sources. Physical calibration is UNKNOWN; acceptance is determined outside the participant. This artefact governs only how I order experiments, read observations and choose among designs. It is not a device assignment and it never edits the task, physics, initial state, event, source access, evaluator or budget.

STEP 0 (entry). Call inspect once. Record: service (application_bytes, event_time_s, receive_deadline_s, unique_valid_frames), legal_design_ranges, current_design, current_measurement, retained_failures, partition/scope, and the episode budget (candidate executions, distinct designs, tool_calls, requests, wall_seconds). Treat budget numbers as hard costs to be reported, not as targets to be used up.

STEP 1 (acquire and fingerprint). Acquire every listed source; record source_sha256 and the acquisition block (bytes, native_calls, new_scientific_executions, wall_seconds) as actual cost. Then write an explicit fingerprint of the fields that bound the design: event_latch kind, cap_initial_voltage_v, capacitance_f, ready_v, off_v, cap_voltage_max_v, boot_j, boot_delay_s, esr_ohm, output_v, tx_current_a, tx_duration_s, off_power_w, idle_power_w, harvest_efficiency, plus the whole source_segments list (start_s, end_s, power_w), dt_s, contact_duration_s, deadline_s and any shunts. RULE: no number, band, limit, or scenario conclusion computed in a previous episode is reused, even when the model id matches. Retained evidence that this rule is load-bearing: episodes recorded under the same model id differ in event_latch ('volatile' vs 'passive-mechanical'), in source structure (two segments 0-0.006 s at 16.667 mW and 0.03-0.06 s at 3.667 mW with a 40 uJ shunt at 0.012 s, versus one segment 0-0.02 s at 7.5 mW with no shunt), and in the capacitance default (1e-5 F vs 2.2e-5 F). Any band carried across would have been wrong. If a source or field is unavailable, record it as UNKNOWN together with which later rules become unavailable; never substitute a remembered value.

STEP 2 (terminality-first reading, before diagnosis). 2.1 Mark a delivery ACHIEVED iff a packet exists with application_bytes equal to service.application_bytes, one unique event id equal to the service event, and packet time <= receive_deadline_s. 2.2 Define the post-terminal region of a trace as all activity strictly after the last tx-complete (or after the last source-segment end when no transmission occurred). Post-terminal brownouts, spills, reboots and idles are expected decay: record them, do not diagnose them, and never let them justify a knob change or an execution. 2.3 Only an absent ACHIEVED packet, or an ACHIEVED packet that violates a service field, is a retained failure. Classify it as: (a) deadline miss; (b) no boot / never reached ready voltage; (c) brownout or reset before tx-complete (transient-transmission); (d) frame-shape violation (bytes, uniqueness, count, duplicates); (e) latch loss between capture and transmission. 2.4 Preserve failed checks, tool errors, unavailable actions and UNKNOWNs verbatim; never re-label a failure or an unknown as a success, and never let a later episode's outcome rewrite an earlier one.

STEP 3 (predictor stated on the recorded grid, before any execution is spent). Use the recorded dt_s and mirror the model's order of operations with discrete steps rather than a closed-form shortcut. Setup: e0 = 0.5*C*cap_initial_voltage_v^2. Per tick k at time t_k: input = (sum of segment power covering t_k)*harvest_efficiency; drain = off_power_w while not yet booted, else idle_power_w, plus tx_current_a*output_v while transmitting; e <- e + (input - drain)*dt, clamped at 0.5*C*cap_voltage_max_v^2 and floored at 0. Boot at the first k with e >= 0.5*C*ready_v^2, then e <- e - boot_j and t_boot = k*dt + boot_delay_s. Transmit when booted, t >= tx_not_before_s, and e >= 0.5*C*ready_v^2; during transmission, treat loaded_v = output_v + esr_ohm*tx_current_a as the sustaining requirement, i.e. a reset occurs if e would fall below 0.5*C*loaded_v^2 before tx_duration_s elapses. Record t_boot, t_ready, t_done and three margins with numbers: (i) deadline margin = receive_deadline_s - t_done; (ii) transmission energy margin = e at tx start - 0.5*C*loaded_v^2 - (tx_current_a*output_v*tx_duration_s - input credit over the tx window); (iii) spill margin = 0.5*C*cap_voltage_max_v^2 - peak e over [t_capture, t_done]. Why the discrete form is mandatory: in a retained episode the closed form ceil((E_ready + boot_j)/charge_step) predicted 0.0166 s against an observed 0.0158 s (eight ticks off) while charging to the ready threshold first and only then subtracting boot_j matched within one tick. The defect was in the formula, not in the design, so the predictor is itself a falsifiable artefact.

STEP 4 (validate the predictor before selecting). If a retained trace exists whose fingerprint from STEP 1 matches the currently acquired sources, recompute that trace with STEP 3 and require agreement within two dt ticks on t_boot and t_done. If no fingerprint match exists, label the predictor's absolute times UNKNOWN and use it only for the sign of differences between candidate designs (monotonicity in capacitance and in the timing floor). A mismatch beyond two ticks is a predictor failure: fix the formula, re-derive, and never move a knob to absorb a modelling error.

STEP 5 (selection under the failure-class -> direction rule). 5.1 If a retained observation is ACHIEVED and current_design satisfies (i)-(iii) with recorded positive margins, keep it and spend no execution; spend nothing to suppress decay that occurs after transmission is complete. 5.2 Otherwise change exactly one legal knob, in the direction the sign of the violated inequality demands, re-evaluate all three inequalities, and only then spend one candidate execution. Never change two knobs in one execution; never change a knob in response to a post-terminal event; keep the timing floor at the earliest legal setting unless a recorded failure class names a capture gate, because a late floor both spends idle energy and pushes t_done toward the deadline while the source may be dark. 5.3 Among designs satisfying (i)-(iii), take the maximin of the three normalised margins and state in one line why each rejected edge fails. Direction evidence retained, not assumed: a design combining a small capacitance, a floor near the legal maximum and a latch that does not survive a reset produced zero frames, with the event captured at 0.0037-0.0079 s then destroyed by an energy-threshold brownout at 0.0121 s and a reboot at 0.0381 s reporting event_was_captured=false; a design keeping the earliest legal floor instead delivered one 8-byte frame at 0.0158 s with zero pre-deadline brownouts. 5.4 Never present the chosen candidate as the method: the method is this procedure, and the candidate is a separate artefact belonging to the design role, which this role neither submits nor checks.

STEP 6 (bounded verification, no duplicate transport). Spend at most one design check per distinct design and at most one send attempt per distinct payload. If design checking is unavailable (ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE), record the candidate as UNVERIFIED/UNKNOWN, keep the arithmetic as the only evidence, and do not spend budget re-routing the same payload through another action; a retained episode lost its residual budget by re-sending an identical payload after a limit error. If a budget error appears (e.g. EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT), the legal remainder is a no-update that states the reason, the residual budget and what remains UNKNOWN, never a relabelled retry.

STEP 7 (report and retain). Report input versions by source_sha256, the fingerprint, the predictor's numbers and the three margins, what was actually observed, every UNKNOWN, and the actual acquisition/execution cost. Keep all prior retained failures verbatim alongside this episode's status. Make no claim of hardware validity, statistical advantage, method migration, recursive self-improvement or external acceptance.
